metadata.summary: England have hit back at Eddie Jones' claim they could be vulnerable to an upset by Japan on Saturday because they have one eye on their upcoming game with New Zealand.
metadata.content: England respond to Eddie Jones mind games ahead of Japan match in Nations Championship | Rugby Union News | Sky Sports Skip to main content England respond to Eddie Jones mind games ahead of Japan match in Nations Championship England scrum coach Tom Harrison denied his side will be distracted by their upcoming game against New Zealand ahead of facing Eddie Jones' Japan on Saturday at Twickenham; Cadan Murley looking to play his "best rugby" and hold down place in starting line-up Friday 13 November 2026 17:10, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' James Cole previews the Nations Championship game between England and Japan as Eddie Jones returns to Twickenham. England have hit back at Eddie Jones' claim they could be vulnerable to an upset by Japan on Saturday because they have one eye on their upcoming game with New Zealand. Jones is aiming to disrupt Steve Borthwick's side by hitting them with the unexpected in the belief they will be "a little bit distracted" by the All Blacks' visit to Allianz Stadium on November 21. New Zealand are the box-office fixture of the campaign ahead of finals weekend but England deny they are looking beyond Japan. Pochettino has been appointed as Michael Carrick's replacement at Old Trafford having signed a deal until the summer of 2029. It comes mere months after extending his stay with the USMNT until the 2030 World Cup. The Argentine will begin his new role on November 18, after taking charge of the USA's two fixtures against Haiti. Viddal Riley will put himself on a path to a cruiserweight world title shot, if he can defend the European championship against Seydi Coupe on Saturday. Only 14 fights into his pro career, Riley is already rated as the IBF's No. 2 contender for their world championship. The Londoner wants to showcase himself as a world champion in waiting against Coupe. "I think I'm the most well-rounded cruiserweight in the world," Riley told Sky Sports . "I think we've trained for that because we want to cover every aspect of the game. We don't want to be lacking any area when it comes to movement, speed, IQ. All these things, I have them." metadata.summary: Harry Cobden made his first ride on Jonbon in public a successful one as the odds-on favourite landed a third Shloer Chase in gritty fashion at Cheltenham.
metadata.content: Cheltenham: Jonbon records Shloer Chase hat-trick for Nicky Henderson | Racing News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Cheltenham: Jonbon records Shloer Chase hat-trick for Nicky Henderson The evergreen Jonbon continued his record of never finishing outside the first two places when seeing off Mighty Bandit to land a third Shloer Chase crown at Cheltenham for Nicky Henderson and JP McManus Friday 13 November 2026 16:04, UK Image: Jonbon - a three-time winner of the Shloer Chase Harry Cobden made his first ride on Jonbon in public a successful one as the odds-on favourite landed a third Shloer Chase in gritty fashion at Cheltenham. Never out of the first two in 29 races, Nicky Henderson's charge is approaching veteran status at the age of 10 and was winning for the 21st time in his stellar career. His task was made easier with the late withdrawal of Gidleigh Park, but Mighty Bandit kept him honest after the last, with the 1-2 favourite pulling away again towards to line to win by two and a quarter lengths. Cobden said: "I'm so fortunate to be in this position riding all of these great horses and there's so many in the camp to look forward to, you do have to pinch yourself a little bit. "I was really looking forward to it and pressure is just something you put on yourself isn't it. There was no point having a sleepless night over a Shloer Chase though as what would I be like in March!" He went on: "I really enjoyed that. metadata.summary: Elina Svitolina defeated Aryna Sabalenka over three compelling sets to reach the semi-finals of the WTA Finals in Indian Wells.
metadata.content: WTA Finals: Elina Svitolina defeats Aryna Sabalenka to reach semi-finals as Mirra Andreeva overwhelms Diana Shnaider | Tennis News | Sky Sports Skip to main content WTA Finals: Elina Svitolina defeats Aryna Sabalenka to reach semi-finals as Mirra Andreeva overwhelms Diana Shnaider Elina Svitolina has eliminated Aryna Sabalenka from the WTA Finals, winning in three sets, 6-3 ⁠3-6 ​6-1 after momentum swung from one to the other and back; Svitolina will face Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova in the semi-finals at Indian Wells Tennis Garden Saturday 14 November 2026 00:07, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of Aryna Sabalenka against Elina Svitolina in the WTA Finals. Elina Svitolina defeated Aryna Sabalenka over three compelling sets to reach the semi-finals of the WTA Finals in Indian Wells. The Ukrainian won 6-3 ⁠3-6 ​6-1, standing up to Sabalenka's powerful serve as she won the first set. Sabalenka stormed back to take control of the second set. But momentum shifted yet again in the deciding set. The opening games of the third were tight, but Svitolina landed a hammer blow when she broke Sabalenka's service game to go 3-1 up and pressed on from there to run away with the final set. "Very happy with the performance. It was not an easy match. It was a little bit of a roller coaster," Svitolina told Sky Sports .
